clue.text: Exasperated journalist leaving, going after dosh

indicators.note: going after places the journalist and the leaving word behind the money

parts.note: dosh and brass are both British slang for money
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
someone leaving is off, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: An irritated reporter quits the job and goes off chasing cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed up and annoyed is the British idiom for being exasperated.

clue.text: Physicist's brother regularly appearing

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word brother shows up, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A scientist's sibling keeps turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'brother'; the 's after Physicist is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish physicist who modelled the atom's electron shells.

clue.text: Area seen as holy with sides going out

indicators.note: the outer letters of the synonym for holy are dropped, its sides removed

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: A patch of land is regarded as sacred, its edges falling away.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: Plant description Violet Elizabeth wouldn't have recognised?

definitions.text: Plant description Violet Elizabeth wouldn't have recognised?

parts.words: Plant description Violet Elizabeth wouldn't have recognised?
parts.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott, the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William books, would have said 'thweet' for the flower's first word, and its second word is the boy she pursued

explanation.surface: A flower name that a lisping storybook girl could never have pronounced properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott, from the British Just William children's stories, lisps ('I'll thcream and thcream'), so she could not say this garden flower's name as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a cottage-garden pink, Dianthus barbatus, so the flower is the plant described.

clue.text: Sink when swallowing river?

indicators.note: the word for sink takes the river letter inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: to sink a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: Going under while gulping down river water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes drowning: going under while swallowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: To die by going under and swallowing water is to perish in the way the clue pictures.

clue.text: Like bird protected by parent — first from eggs nestling

indicators.note: the letter from eggs settles inside the other piece, like a chick in a nest

parts.note: to father a child is to care for it as a parent, so one protected by a parent has been fathered

indicators.note: only the opening letter of eggs is taken

explanation.surface: A chick sheltered by its mother or father, the first to hatch from the clutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds alone have plumage, so a creature covered in plumage is bird-like.

clue.text: Pen to stop functioning

definitions.meaning: a business that collapses or ceases trading is said to do this

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sheepfold enclosure and the verb for a business closing down.

clue.text: One like Macmillan led nation rebuilding — nothing to it!

indicators.note: to it says the nothing letter is attached to the rebuilt letters

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: the letters of led and nation are rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister like Macmillan led the nation's recovery, and it was effortless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' rearranges LEDNATION to LDETONIAN, and O goes in front. Harold Macmillan, British prime minister 1957-63, went to Eton.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan was a former pupil of Eton College, so another alumnus is one like him.

clue.text: Fear what may be met on boat trips? They're pretty hairy!

parts.note: dread means fear

parts.words: what may be met on boat trips
parts.note: canal and river boats pass through locks

explanation.surface: A nervous passenger on a canal cruise faces some scary moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks like slang for scary, but here it means literally covered in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Matted ropes of hair are a hairstyle, so the plural hairstyle is literally full of hair.

clue.text: Female moving up?

parts.note: moving up reads as social climbing, but means climbing into the saddle as a rider mounts

explanation.surface: A woman climbing the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman rider mounts her animal, literally moving up onto its back.

clue.text: Fish going around lake without purpose

indicators.note: the fish's name surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: A fish swims aimlessly round and round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean pointless or done for no reason, as in idle threats.

clue.text: Part of course giving indication of good posture?

definitions.meaning: the stretch of a racecourse on the far side from the finishing post
read literally, a spine held upright

explanation.definitionFit: On a racecourse the far-side stretch has this name, and a literal reading describes an upright spine.

clue.text: Very cruel son — one boy to pass judgement on another

parts.note: Tony is a boy's name
a judge hears a case before ruling on it
another boy, Ted

explanation.surface: A son behaves very cruelly, as one boy sits in judgement on another.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a heart like stone shows no pity, which is very cruel.

clue.text: Dubious value with bad person in show

indicators.note: the bad person is placed inside the rearranged letters
dubious suggests the word value is not to be trusted as it stands, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a devil is a wicked person

explanation.surface: A show of dubious worth featuring a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' looks like a comment on the show's worth, but it rearranges the five letters of value before the villain is placed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a variety show of music-hall acts, chiefly American.

clue.text: Dress with sweat inappropriate for working woman

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweaty outfit is unsuitable for a woman at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An air hostess or ship's attendant is a woman whose job is looking after passengers.

clue.text: Loss of rights making a trained teacher initially wild

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of teacher is taken
wild signals the preceding letters running riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A qualified teacher who goes wild ends up stripped of rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was the old legal forfeiture of civil rights and property after a sentence for treason or felony.

clue.text: Anger in place restricted by illness

indicators.note: the place abbreviation is hemmed in by the word for illness

parts.note: illness means disease
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Fury at being confined to one spot by sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to annoy or displease them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fencing to finish in decisive result

indicators.note: the finishing word goes inside the knockout abbreviation

parts.note: KO, a knockout, settles a boxing bout decisively
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A fencing match is fought to a conclusive finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Peg has 80% of widow's inheritance left

indicators.note: four letters out of five are kept, losing the last of the widow's share

parts.note: a dower is the share of a dead husband's estate due to his widow

explanation.surface: A peg makes up most of what a widow is left in the will.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden pin or peg used to join pieces of wood.

clue.text: Manager finally in change of course after team gets draw away

indicators.note: after puts the changed course behind the team

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: the manager's last letter goes inside the word for a change of course

parts.note: a sailing boat tacks to change course

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Manager is taken

explanation.surface: A team manager makes a late tactical switch while the side is distracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw away' means divert someone's attention; the course change is a sailing tack, with the manager's last letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to divert or lead them away from their main purpose.

clue.text: One not shining consistently in arts maybe?

parts.note: the letters of arts are a variable version of star, a changed arrangement of it

explanation.surface: Someone in the humanities whose brilliance comes and goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: a 'variable star' is a scrambled STAR, such as ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call a star whose brightness fluctuates over time by this name.

clue.text: Military honour for male in a particular battle

indicators.note: for signals that the medal letters take the place of the male letter

parts.note: some, as in 'some person', means a particular one
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A soldier is decorated for valour in one particular battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In SOME, the M for 'male' is swapped for MM, the Military Medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme was a First World War battle in northern France in 1916.

clue.text: Ball needing announcement of important person

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a nob is British slang for a person of high rank or wealth

explanation.surface: A grand dance needs a dignitary to be announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance but means a round lump, like a knob of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob is a rounded lump or handle, so a ball shape fits.

clue.text: Magnificent musical ending

definitions.meaning: the Italian marking in a score showing where a piece ends

explanation.definitionFit: The word means splendid, and in sheet music it is the Italian marking for the end of a piece.

clue.text: It's right being slim, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard, pointing to a word that sounds like another

parts.note: slim means lean

explanation.surface: Being thin is a good thing, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Hotchpotch amusing lad inordinately

indicators.note: inordinately means beyond proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jumble produced by a boy who is excessively entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmagundi is a mixed salad dish, and figuratively any miscellaneous mixture.

clue.text: One of four at table having beano without starter

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its starter

parts.note: a beano is British slang for a party or feast

explanation.surface: A diner joins a party meal but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The four at the table are bridge players, named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and this is one seat.

clue.text: Charming Democrat not hopeless as candidate

parts.note: a candidate who could win at the polls is electable

explanation.surface: A charismatic Democrat has a real chance of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or highly pleasing, close to charming.
